prov_bang_tam.name: Băng Tâm
prov_bang_tam.lore: Red badlands, dry steppe and the first snow mountains meet around the seat of Băng Tâm Các. Herders, well-diggers and the sect's own servants live here, and the land yields little but stone, wool and qi. Disciples drink only the seat's ice-cold well water, and the head keeps a retreat in the hills behind it.

prov_da_quang.name: Dạ Quang
prov_da_quang.lore: Steppe, sand and salt pans run to the coast around the red-earth fort of Dạ Quang Môn. Its riders and horse-breeders guard the caravans they once robbed, and the land yields horses, salt and the pale stone of the night-glowing cups. The broken fortress of Cô Thành stands on its salt pan, a reminder of the Desert Road War.

prov_p116.name: Ngư Đàm
prov_p116.lore: Dry steppe around an oasis of fish ponds beside a barren salt sea. Its people raise carp and dates and send live fish to the seat in water jars. An Earth vein lies under the pond fields.

prov_p117.name: Liên Đường
prov_p117.lore: A small green hollow of spring-fed grassland on the coast. Its people live on lotus root and seed and on what caravans spend when they stop to look. Dạ Quang's riders water their horses here and leave the flowers alone.

prov_p118.name: Mã Minh
prov_p118.lore: Grassland behind the range where herders have run horses since 100. They sell remounts to Băng Tâm's caravans and anyone who pays. The old wells to the west lie under the sand of 1050.

prov_p35.name: Trường Vân
prov_p35.lore: Steppe and grassland around the river mouth where Trường Vân Thành stands, Băng Tâm's door to the sea since 470. Caravan guards, chandlers and the sect's officers fill it, and goods pass from camel to ship under the long gallery. Its guard families have never forgiven Hạng Dạ Bôi, who was born among them.

prov_p67.name: Hồi Lan
prov_p67.lore: Steppe running to the desert coast behind the hooked breakwater of Hồi Lan Thành. Southern ships trade here for wool, salt and northern furs. A warm spring in the steppe is where the merchants bathe off the road dust.

prov_r8_1.name: Xích Nham Lĩnh
prov_r8_1.lore: Red-rocked mountains between the ice range and the desert. No one lives here now; turquoise is mined in the hills. The burned stockade of Dạ Quang's raider days still stands in a side valley.

prov_r8_10.name: Hoàng Sa Nguyên
prov_r8_10.lore: Dry steppe that turns into open dunes in the south. No village stands here; caravans cross it in two days and do not stop. Golden scorpions hunt in the dunes.

prov_r8_11.name: Sạn Đạo Lĩnh
prov_r8_11.lore: High mountains, badlands and desert cut by the gorge of Viên Đề Hạp and its plank road. No sect holds the road and no one lives here; caravans cross with wax in their ears. Copper-red rock and dry slopes surround the gorge.

prov_r8_12.name: Hãn Hải Mạc
prov_r8_12.lore: Open desert with a few bare hills and badland ridges. No one lives here but at a boiling spring in the sand, where caravans water their beasts. Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars there for travellers.

prov_r8_13.name: Lưu Sa Câu
prov_r8_13.lore: Desert cut by a thin river whose bed shifts every year. Wild camels graze the river edge, and no one settles here. Caravans follow the river and pay for guides who know where the sand is soft.

prov_r8_14.name: Chiên Trướng
prov_r8_14.lore: Wide steppe with some desert and badland to the south. Its herders live in felt tents, move with their flocks and make felt for the seat and the caravans. A Fire vein lies in the desert edge.

prov_r8_15.name: Chử Diêm
prov_r8_15.lore: Coastal steppe running down to a salt shore. Its people boil sea water into salt over dung fires and sell it to the caravans and to Hồi Lan. A bitter hot spring rises inland.

prov_r8_2.name: Hàn Tùng Lĩnh
prov_r8_2.lore: Pine-covered mountains on the north edge of the desert. Coal is dug here for the seat's forges. The ruin of a small sect that died in the Desert Road War lies in the pines.

prov_r8_3.name: Mộc Kiều
prov_r8_3.lore: A river valley of forest and steppe below the mountains. Its people log, farm a little and keep the timber bridge on the road from the seat to the coast. Silver foxes live in the woods above.

prov_r8_4.name: Ngọc Môn Lĩnh
prov_r8_4.lore: Very high mountains, over four and a half thousand metres, at the west end of the desert. White jade is mined at their foot. The old poem of Cô Thành looks toward the jade gate, and caravan drivers say this is it.

prov_r8_5.name: Đà Linh
prov_r8_5.lore: Steppe and desert along a river under the mountains, where caravans gather before the long crossing. Camel breeders, harness makers and innkeepers live in its town. A sandstorm-swept Earth vein lies to the west.

prov_r8_6.name: Lạc Nhật Nguyên
prov_r8_6.lore: Half steppe and half desert along a long river, where the lone smoke of caravan fires rises straight in still air. No one settles here. A Fire vein lies where the sun sets over the river.

prov_r8_7.name: Mục Dương
prov_r8_7.lore: Steppe with patches of desert and red badland in the east. Its people herd sheep and goats and sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. An Earth vein lies under a low rise.

prov_r8_8.name: Tuyết Hải Lĩnh
prov_r8_8.lore: Huge mountains with small glaciers rise over the west of the desert. No one lives here. The empty fort of Băng Tâm's first ice keepers stands in a pass.

prov_r8_9.name: Liệt Thạch Lĩnh
prov_r8_9.lore: Mountains and red badlands split by heat and frost. No one lives here, and the old caravan fort lies under sand. Snakes and scorpions shelter in the cracks.

prov_bang_tam_spirit_vein_1.name: Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền
prov_bang_tam_spirit_vein_1.look: A cold spring wells up in a rock basin on the mountainside, its stone rim cut with long grooves where blades have been laid.
prov_bang_tam_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Metal vein rises here with the water. Băng Tâm's sword cultivators wash a new sword in it before they first draw it in earnest.

prov_da_quang_spirit_vein_1.name: Xích Sa Mạch
prov_da_quang_spirit_vein_1.look: A patch of red sand in the desert that stays hot after sunset, shimmering faintly in the dark.
prov_da_quang_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Fire vein lies under the red sand. Dạ Quang's riders temper their blood sabres here, and Băng Tâm lets them.

prov_p116_spirit_vein_1.name: Hoàng Thổ Mạch
prov_p116_spirit_vein_1.look: A low mound of yellow earth among the fish ponds, where the grass grows thicker than anywhere in the desert.
prov_p116_spirit_vein_1.lore: An Earth vein lies under the pond fields. The villagers say it is why their fish grow so fat.

prov_p117_lake_1.name: Lục Ba Đàm
prov_p117_lake_1.look: A clear spring-fed pool among grass, its surface rippling green with lotus leaves.
prov_p117_lake_1.lore: This is the largest of the Liên Đường ponds and the source of the rest. Dạ Quang's riders water horses at its lower end only.

prov_p118_spirit_vein_1.name: Mục Thảo Mạch
prov_p118_spirit_vein_1.look: A meadow on the steppe where the grass stays green even in drought, crossed by horse trails.
prov_p118_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein lies under the meadow. Mã Minh's herders graze their best mares here.

prov_p35_spirit_vein_1.name: Quy Vân Mạch
prov_p35_spirit_vein_1.look: A low rise on the steppe where morning mist gathers and lingers until noon.
prov_p35_spirit_vein_1.lore: An Earth vein lies under the rise, and its qi draws the mist. Trường Vân's guards say the long clouds over the mountains come home here.

prov_p35_minor_seat_p.name: Trấn Sa Đường
prov_p35_minor_seat_p.look: A walled compound of pale mud brick on a rise in the steppe, with a sabre yard and a long stable.
prov_p35_minor_seat_p.lore: The caravan guard families of Trường Vân founded this hall in 1125, after Dạ Quang Môn was made to guard the caravans. They train guards in sabre and desert craft, and they watch Dạ Quang's riders more closely than the road.

sect.name: Trấn Sa Đường
sect.craft: caravan guards and desert sabre arts

prov_p67_hot_spring_1.name: Ôn Thạch Thang
prov_p67_hot_spring_1.look: Warm water fills a ring of smooth stones in the steppe, steaming in the cold mornings.
prov_p67_hot_spring_1.lore: Hồi Lan's merchants bathe here to wash off the road. The spring's mild Fire qi is good for joints stiffened by the desert cold.

prov_r8_1_peak_1.name: Thạch Kiếm Phong
prov_r8_1_peak_1.look: A tall blade of red rock stands upright on the ridge.
prov_r8_1_peak_1.lore: Its Metal qi draws Băng Tâm's sword cultivators. The raiders of Dạ Quang used it as a lookout.

prov_r8_1_mine_2.name: Tùng Thạch Khoáng
prov_r8_1_mine_2.look: Small pits dot a red hillside, with chips of blue-green stone in the spoil.
prov_r8_1_mine_2.lore: Turquoise is dug here for ornaments and caravan trade. Desert people say it guards a rider from falling.

prov_r8_1_ruin_3.name: Huyết Đao Trại
prov_r8_1_ruin_3.look: A burned stockade of red stone and timber in a side valley, its walls blackened and its gate burned out.
prov_r8_1_ruin_3.lore: Dạ Quang's raiders hid their loot here from 975. Băng Tâm burned it in 1121 when it marched on them, and Hạng Dạ Bôi knelt soon after.

prov_r8_10_beast_lair_1.name: Kim Hạt Cương
prov_r8_10_beast_lair_1.look: A ridge of yellow dunes pocked with holes, and golden shells glinting in the sand at noon.
prov_r8_10_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit scorpions with golden shells hunt here at night. Their poison is sold to alchemists, and the men who catch them rarely live to old age.

prov_r8_12_hot_spring_1.name: Phí Sa Thang
prov_r8_12_hot_spring_1.look: Hot water bubbles up through the sand into a shallow pool ringed with white crust.
prov_r8_12_hot_spring_1.lore: Fire qi rises with the water. Caravans water their camels here after it cools, and Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars beside it.

prov_r8_13_beast_lair_1.name: Dã Đà Nguyên
prov_r8_13_beast_lair_1.look: Flat sand along the river, tracked by broad two-toed hoofprints and dotted with dung.
prov_r8_13_beast_lair_1.lore: Wild spirit camels graze the river edge, led by a white bull. Caravan breeders try to catch its calves.

prov_r8_14_village_1.name: Chiên Trướng Thôn
prov_r8_14_village_1.look: A ring of round felt tents on the steppe, with felt drying on frames and flocks grazing all around.
prov_r8_14_village_1.lore: The herders move the village twice a year. They make felt for the seat's winter halls and the caravans.

prov_r8_14_spirit_vein_2.name: Liệt Dương Huyệt
prov_r8_14_spirit_vein_2.look: A bowl of red rock in the desert where the air shimmers even in winter.
prov_r8_14_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Fire vein rises here. Băng Tâm's disciples come to train the ice heart against heat.

prov_r8_15_village_1.name: Chử Diêm Thôn
prov_r8_15_village_1.look: Low mud houses on a salt shore, with iron pans steaming over dung fires along the waterline.
prov_r8_15_village_1.lore: The villagers boil sea water into salt and sell it to caravans and to Hồi Lan. Every child learns to tend a pan before they can read.

prov_r8_15_hot_spring_2.name: Khổ Thủy Trì
prov_r8_15_hot_spring_2.look: A warm pool in the steppe, its water cloudy and its edges stained white and yellow.
prov_r8_15_hot_spring_2.lore: Its water is too bitter to drink, but salt-boilers soak their cracked hands in it. Its Fire qi is weak and its Water qi bitter.

prov_r8_2_peak_1.name: Hạc Lập Phong
prov_r8_2_peak_1.look: A slim grey peak rises alone above the pines like a crane standing on one leg.
prov_r8_2_peak_1.lore: Its Metal qi is mild and steady. The ruined sect below once held its morning practice here.

prov_r8_2_mine_2.name: Hắc Môi Khoáng
prov_r8_2_mine_2.look: Black spoil heaps and a timber headframe stand among pines at the foot of the mountain.
prov_r8_2_mine_2.lore: Coal is dug here for the forges of the seat. The miners' faces are always black, and they are called the crows.

prov_r8_2_ruin_3.name: Lãnh Hương Các
prov_r8_2_ruin_3.look: A small ruined pavilion among pines, its roof fallen and a grove of wild plum gone feral around it.
prov_r8_2_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of plum-blossom sword cultivators founded this pavilion in 600. In 724 all its disciples rode to break the siege of Cô Thành and none came back.

prov_r8_3_village_1.name: Mộc Kiều Thôn
prov_r8_3_village_1.look: Log houses on both banks of a river, joined by a long timber bridge on stone piers.
prov_r8_3_village_1.lore: The village keeps the bridge on the road from the seat to the coast, and Băng Tâm pays it in grain. Its loggers fell timber in the hills above.

prov_r8_3_beast_lair_2.name: Ngân Hồ Lâm
prov_r8_3_beast_lair_2.look: A forested slope with fox earths between the roots and silver hairs caught on the bark.
prov_r8_3_beast_lair_2.lore: Silver spirit foxes live here and steal from the village. Mộc Kiều's people leave them a share of grain to keep them from the houses.

prov_r8_4_peak_1.name: Tuyết Tôn Phong
prov_r8_4_peak_1.look: A massive white summit over four and a half thousand metres high, towering above the western desert.
prov_r8_4_peak_1.lore: Its Metal and Water qi are fierce. Few have reached the top, and Băng Tâm's elders climb it before a breakthrough.

prov_r8_4_mine_2.name: Dương Chi Khoáng
prov_r8_4_mine_2.look: A mine in a dry stream bed where white stones like congealed fat lie in the gravel.
prov_r8_4_mine_2.lore: White jade is dug from the stream bed and the cliffs above. Băng Tâm carves its seals from it.

prov_r8_5_town_1.name: Đà Linh Trấn
prov_r8_5_town_1.look: A river town of mud-brick inns and camel yards, ringing with camel bells.
prov_r8_5_town_1.lore: Caravans gather here before the long crossing. The town makes the bronze bells every caravan camel wears.

prov_r8_5_spirit_vein_2.name: Phong Sa Nhãn
prov_r8_5_spirit_vein_2.look: A ring of standing stones in the desert, where small whirlwinds of sand rise even on still days.
prov_r8_5_spirit_vein_2.lore: An Earth vein lies under the ring. The caravan drivers of Đà Linh say storms are born here.

prov_r8_6_spirit_vein_1.name: Viên Nhật Huyệt
prov_r8_6_spirit_vein_1.look: A round hollow on the steppe by the river, its red earth glowing as if the setting sun lay in it.
prov_r8_6_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Fire vein rises here. The old caravan song says the long river and the round setting sun meet in this hollow.

prov_r8_7_village_1.name: Mục Dương Thôn
prov_r8_7_village_1.look: Stone pens and low houses on the steppe, ringed by grazing sheep.
prov_r8_7_village_1.lore: The shepherds sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. They count sheep at dusk with a song that no outsider understands.

prov_r8_7_spirit_vein_2.name: Bàn Thạch Mạch
prov_r8_7_spirit_vein_2.look: A flat slab of rock as big as a courtyard on a steppe rise, warm to the touch.
prov_r8_7_spirit_vein_2.lore: An Earth vein lies under the slab. Shepherds sleep on it in winter.

prov_r8_8_peak_1.name: Băng Quan Phong
prov_r8_8_peak_1.look: A huge peak capped with a crown of ice above the desert.
prov_r8_8_peak_1.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the ice. Băng Tâm's ice cultivators come to sit in its cold.

prov_r8_8_ruin_2.name: Ngưng Băng Bảo
prov_r8_8_ruin_2.look: Low mounds of slumped ice and stone stand in a high pass, the shape of walls still visible.
prov_r8_8_ruin_2.lore: Tần Ngưng Sương's first disciples built this fort of ice blocks in 450 to guard the pass, keeping it frozen with their arts. When she died in 1010 no one renewed the ice, and the walls slumped.

prov_r8_9_peak_1.name: Hồng Thạch Phong
prov_r8_9_peak_1.look: A cracked red peak above the badlands, split by heat and frost.
prov_r8_9_peak_1.lore: Its Earth qi is heavy and dry. Snakes shelter in its cracks.

prov_r8_9_ruin_2.name: Mai Sa Bảo
prov_r8_9_ruin_2.look: Only the top of a watch tower shows above a dune in a mountain pass.
prov_r8_9_ruin_2.lore: Băng Tâm built this caravan fort in 600. The sandstorm of 1050 that buried Mã Minh's wells buried it too, and it was not dug out.
